institution: Sorbonne Université (Faculté des Sciences et Ingénierie), in collaboration with IRCAM and Télécom Paris
programme: M2 ATIAM — Acoustique, Traitement du signal, Informatique, Appliqués à la Musique
stillExists: YES. Running and recruiting. The application page publishes a live calendar for the 2026-2027 intake (application window 26 March – 11 June 2026, results by July, start early September 2026). No sign of discontinuation.
awards: A real second-cycle degree — but only the SECOND YEAR of one. ATIAM is an M2 (fifth year) within Sorbonne Université's national master's. Sorbonne Université's own fee page states the master's rate: "For master's degree programmes, the tuition fee is €255 for the 2026-2027 academic year." The diploma is the French Diplôme National de Master.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: NO — not at this level. The page requires an already-completed FIRST year of a master's: "niveau de maîtrise ou master M1 en informatique ou mathématiques" (for the IT profile) or "master 1 en physique/acoustique" (for the acoustics/signal profile). Engineering-school diploma holders (diplôme d'ingénieur, bac+5) are also eligible. A three-year BSc is bac+3 and is two years short.
liveAudition: NO live audition. The gate is (1) a dossier via Sorbonne's eCandidat and (2) "Entretien de motivation" — a motivation interview held at IRCAM. It is an academic interview, not a performance audition and not a portfolio review. But it probes signal-processing/CS competence at M1 level.
portfolioSpec: There is NO artistic portfolio requirement. The dossier is academic: transcripts, CV, a motivation letter that must explicitly state interest in ATIAM, and optional recommendation letters. Selection criteria quoted: "un niveau similaire à celui atteint à l'issue d'une première année de master" in one or two of the core subjects, plus motivation/musical interest and "un bon niveau d'anglais."
costForTunisian: Sorbonne Université national master rate 255 €/yr (verified on the university's own enrolment page). Differentiated fees (droits différenciés) DO formally apply to non-EU students — Sorbonne's page confirms it applies them — but the same page describes automatic full exemptions and an Exemption Committee route. Press reporting (12 July 2026) says the Sorbonne CA voted unanimously on 7 July 2026 to exonerate all non-EU students so they pay the same as everyone else; the exact differentiated master figure (reported around 3 941 €) is NOT published on Sorbonne's own English fee page — UNVERIFIED on an official page. CVEC is compulsory and paid to CROUS; the amount is not published on that page.
funding: Nothing programme-specific published on the ATIAM candidature page. UNVERIFIED — no ATIAM-run scholarship found. Tunisians would depend on the French Embassy/Campus France BGF (Bourse du Gouvernement Français), which is a separate, earlier application, not automatic on admission.
applicationDeadline: 2026-2027 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE, use as the pattern): applications 26 March – 11 June 2026; interviews at IRCAM (date TBA); results by July; enrolment July–October; start early September. Expect the same March–June window in 2027. IMPORTANT for Tunisia: a Tunisian resident applying to a first enrolment in a French institution must go through Campus France Tunisie / Études en France, whose 'Ne t'arrête pas' cycle typically opens the previous autumn (Oct–Dec) and closes well before the university's own June date — the Études en France dossier is the real binding deadline.
languageOfInstruction: French. "Les cours sont en majorité dispensés en français" — a good level of French is recommended for non-francophones. "Un bon niveau d'anglais" is also a selection criterion. No specific certificate named on this page.
verdictWhy: He is structurally ineligible: ATIAM is an M2 that starts from a completed M1 or a five-year engineering diploma, and he has a three-year BSc. Even if he closed that gap, ATIAM is a hard signal-processing/acoustics research master, not an artist-development programme — it would not build him a career as an electronic music producer. Do not spend an application on it.
correction: The input row implies this is an entry-level master reachable with 'Portfolio only'. Both are wrong. (a) There is NO portfolio at all — the gate is an academic dossier plus a motivation interview. (b) It is an M2 requiring bac+4 (M1 completed), not a two-year master a BSc holder can enter. (c) Cost band 'EUR 1.5k-5k/yr' is misleading: the published Sorbonne master rate is 255 €/yr, and non-EU differentiated fees are subject to a Sorbonne exemption policy.

programme: Master mention Musicologie — parcours Musiques Appliquées aux Arts Visuels (MAAAV), M1 and M2
stillExists: YES. Both M1 and M2 pages are live; the M2 page was updated 16 March 2026 and sits in the 2022-2026 accreditation cycle. Note the accreditation period ends in 2026 — a re-accreditation for the next contract is expected but the 2027 offer is not yet published. Treat the 2027 existence as probable, not confirmed.
awards: A real Diplôme National de Master (bac+5), mention Musicologie. Full second-cycle degree, not a certificate.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: YES on paper for M1 — the M1 page states plainly: "Il faut posséder un diplôme de licence (quelle qu'elle soit)" (any bachelor's degree). But the same page adds a hard artistic condition: "Etre déjà compositeur au moment du recrutement : peu importe le style de musique pratiqué." Required competences include mastery of music notation, orchestration and DAW skills. M2 direct entry requires "avoir effectué un master 1 MAAAV" — so he can only enter at M1.
liveAudition: NO live audition published on either page. Selection is on dossier via the national platform. However the 'must already be a composer' clause plus the notation/orchestration competence list functions as a de-facto artistic screen at dossier stage.
portfolioSpec: Not specified on the university pages — the submission spec lives inside the Mon Master / Études en France dossier. UNVERIFIED as a published spec. What is published is the competence expectation: existing compositional output (any genre), music notation, orchestration, DAW.
costForTunisian: CORRECTED AND MATERIAL. Lyon 2's own fee page for 2026-2027: national master rate "255 €"; droits différenciés for non-EU at master level "3 950 €". Lyon 2's dedicated notice confirms the previous blanket exemption is over: "The transitional procedure put in place by the University's Board of Administration is ending starting fall 2026/2027" and "all non-EU students will be required to pay differentiated tuition, except in very specific cases." So budget 3 950 €/yr, not 255 €. CVEC amount not published on that page (UNVERIFIED).
funding: No programme scholarship published. Exemption from droits différenciés is possible but discretionary and no longer automatic (see above) — it is a request, not a grant, and there is no published amount or deadline. UNVERIFIED beyond that. External route: French Embassy BGF via Campus France Tunisie, separate and earlier.
applicationDeadline: M1 entry is exclusively via the national platform: "Le dépôt des dossiers de candidatures se fait en ligne, exclusivement via la plateforme Mon Master." Mon Master's national window is typically late February to late March each year (PRIOR CYCLE pattern). BUT for a Tunisian resident this is overridden: first enrolment from Tunisia goes through Campus France Tunisie / Études en France, opening the preceding autumn. Exact 2027 dates not yet published — UNVERIFIED.
languageOfInstruction: French only. No English track. No English certificate demanded; a French level (typically B2/DELF or TCF) will be demanded by Études en France. Exact required level not published on the programme page.
verdictWhy: The programme is aimed at people who are already composers — 'Etre déjà compositeur au moment du recrutement' plus music notation and orchestration — and it is about scoring for image, not electronic music production. He would be applying with none of the three stated prerequisites, in French, and now paying 3 950 €/yr because Lyon 2's non-EU exemption ends in 2026/27.
correction: Two corrections. (1) COST: Lyon 2 previously exempted non-EU students; that transitional exemption ENDS for 2026/2027, so a Tunisian now pays droits différenciés of 3 950 €/yr at master level, not the 255 € national rate. (2) GATE: input says 'Portfolio + exam/interview'; no audition or interview is published — the real gate is a dossier plus an unpublished requirement that the applicant is already a practising composer with notation and orchestration skills.

institution: Université de Bretagne Occidentale (UBO), Faculté des Sciences et Techniques
programme: Master Ingénierie de l'image, ingénierie du son — parcours Image et Son
stillExists: YES. Programme page live, last updated 2 March 2026.
awards: Diplôme National de Master — a real second-cycle degree. It is a SCIENCES/ENGINEERING master (domaine Sciences, Technologies, Santé), not an arts master.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE, and weakly. The page states entry is "recrutement post-L3 mention SPI parcours Image & Son ou équivalent" — i.e. a physics/engineering-sciences licence in the same specialism, or equivalent. A software-engineering BSc is arguably 'équivalent' on the computing side but has none of the acoustics/optics/signal physics this cohort is built on. Cohort is capped: "La limitation à 18 étudiants par promotion."
liveAudition: NO audition. The page specifies "Dossier de candidature + entretien" — application file plus an INTERVIEW, for both M1 and M2 entry. It is an academic/motivational interview, not a performance audition and not a portfolio review.
portfolioSpec: NONE published — this is an engineering master and does not ask for a creative portfolio. UNVERIFIED whether any work samples are requested inside the dossier.
costForTunisian: CORRECTED AND MATERIAL. UBO's own notice: master national rate "Inscription en Master : 255 €"; differentiated rate for non-EU "Inscription en Master : 3 950 €". UBO explicitly ended its former blanket partial exemption: exemptions are now discretionary and capped — "dans la limite d'un quota réglementaire de 30 % fixé pour l'année 2026/2027" — and "une admission pédagogique ne vaut pas automatiquement exonération des droits d'inscription." Budget 3 950 €/yr plus CVEC (amount not published on that page).
funding: No programme funding. Only the discretionary droits-différenciés exemption (30% quota, personal-circumstances basis, no published amount or deadline) and regulatory exemption for French-government scholarship holders (BGF). Separate, earlier application via Campus France Tunisie. Input's 'None' is essentially right.
applicationDeadline: M1 via the national platform trouvermonmaster.gouv.fr; M2 via ecandidat.univ-brest.fr. National Mon Master window is typically late Feb–late March (PRIOR CYCLE pattern); exact 2027 dates not published — UNVERIFIED. For a Tunisian resident the binding route is Campus France Tunisie / Études en France, opening the preceding autumn.
languageOfInstruction: French. All programme documentation is French-only; no English track. French certificate will be required by Études en France; exact level not published on the programme page.
verdictWhy: This is a French-language image-and-sound ENGINEERING master built on a physics/SPI licence, with an 18-place cap and an interview — it trains broadcast and audiovisual technicians, not electronic music artists. He would pay 3 950 €/yr with no realistic funding and come out with a technical qualification that does not advance the artist goal.
correction: COST: UBO used to grant a partial exemption to all non-EU students; that is over. For 2026/2027 a Tunisian pays droits différenciés of 3 950 €/yr at master level, with exemption only discretionary and capped at a 30% quota. Also, the input gate 'Portfolio + exam/interview' is wrong on the portfolio — there is no portfolio; it is dossier + entretien.

stillExists: YES. Programme page live, winter-semester start, structure "4 Semester" plus "1 Diplomsemester".
awards: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE. It awards a "Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg" — an institutional diploma from a state film academy, classified as a "Diplomaufbaustudium" (postgraduate diploma course). It is not an accredited second-cycle Bologna master's and carries no ECTS-bearing MA/MFA title. This matters for a student visa and for any later PhD or academic route.
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: CASE-BY-CASE but effectively hostile. The formal entry is a Hochschulzugangsberechtigung ("Sollten Sie keine Allgemeine Hochschulreife/Abitur vorweisen können, gibt es die Möglichkeit, den Zugang … über den sogenannten Begabtenpassus … zu erlangen"). For the postgraduate/Projektstudium route applicants need a prior degree OR substantial professional media experience. The real filter is craft: "Grundkenntnisse in Tonstudiotechnik" and "Arbeitsumgang mit Digital Audio Workstations (DAW)" are demanded.
liveAudition: YES — a multi-stage in-person entrance examination (Aufnahmeprüfung), and it is decisive. The published process: "Einzelgespräche mit den leitenden Dozierenden der jeweiligen Abteilung, die Ausgabe der 72-Stunden-Prüfungsaufgabe sowie das abschließende Gespräch innerhalb des Kolloquiums" — individual interviews with department heads, a 72-hour set practical exam task, and a concluding colloquium. It is not a music audition but it is a live, timed, in-person practical test he cannot bluff.
portfolioSpec: Not published on the pages reached. Work samples are requested inside the online application form. UNVERIFIED — I could not find a page specifying number of works, length or format for Filmton/Sounddesign; the decisive assessed artefact is the 72-hour exam task, not a prior portfolio.
costForTunisian: "1.500€ (Nicht-EU-Bürger)" per year for non-EU citizens (EU students pay €0 for this postgraduate course). Additional semester contributions, Studentenwerk and the compulsory German student health insurance (statutory student rate, roughly €130+/month, amount not published by the academy) are not itemised on the page — UNVERIFIED. Blocked-account proof for the German visa is a separate, much larger requirement.
funding: No programme scholarship published on the reached pages. Input claims 'Partial' — UNVERIFIED; I found no named Filmakademie scholarship for this course. German external routes (DAAD) would be a separate, earlier application, and DAAD study scholarships generally target accredited degree programmes, which this is not.
applicationDeadline: "Bewerbungsfrist ist der 15. Februar" — 15 February each year, for the following winter semester. So for an autumn-2027 start: 15 February 2027. This is a stable recurring pattern (only Motion Design differs, 15 May).
languageOfInstruction: German, with some English: "Deutsch/Englisch im PS". German is required at "Goethe Institut Level B2" (or TestDaF 4 / DSH-2). He has NO German.
verdictWhy: Three independent blockers, any one of which is fatal: it demands German at B2 and he has none; it ends in a Filmakademie Diplom rather than a recognised master's degree; and admission runs through an in-person multi-day entrance exam including a 72-hour practical task that assumes existing studio and DAW craft. It is also film post-production, not electronic music.
correction: DEGREE TYPE: the input treats this as a master-level option. It is not a master's — it awards a "Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg" from a Diplomaufbaustudium, not an accredited second-cycle degree. GATE: 'Exam/interview only' understates it — the exam includes a 72-hour set practical task plus a colloquium, in person. LANGUAGE: German B2 (Goethe B2 / TestDaF 4 / DSH-2) is required and is not flagged in the input.

institution: Ionian University (Corfu) — Dept of Music Studies + Dept of Audio and Visual Arts
programme: ΔΠΜΣ «Τέχνες και Τεχνολογίες του Ήχου» / Interdepartmental MA in Sonic Arts and Audio Technologies
stillExists: DOUBTFUL — no current intake published. The programme is formally established (Senate decision 2279, ΦΕΚ 2935/20.07.2018) and the departmental pages are still up, but the most recent call published anywhere on the official sites is "Προκήρυξη ακαδ. έτους 2022-2023 — Κατάθεση δικαιολογητικών μέχρι 18/09/2022". As of August 2026 no 2023, 2024, 2025 or 2026 call has been published. Treat the programme as dormant until the department confirms otherwise. FLAG: verify by email (audiovisual@ionio.gr) before investing anything.
awards: A real Greek second-cycle degree — a ΔΠΜΣ (Interdepartmental Postgraduate Programme) awarding a Δίπλωμα Μεταπτυχιακών Σπουδών (MA). Three semesters, full-time only, mandatory thesis in semester three, maximum 30 students per year (15 per specialisation).
acceptsSoftwareEngineeringBachelor: YES on the published 2022-23 wording. The call lists as eligible "πτυχιούχοι τμημάτων Μουσικής Τεχνολογίας & Ακουστικής, Φυσικής, Πληροφορικής, Ηλεκτρονικής ή Ηλεκτρολογίας" — informatics (Πληροφορικής) graduates are explicitly named for the audio-technology specialisation. Other fields are permitted if the applicant shows "ικανή ερευνητική ή/και καλλιτεχνική δραστηριότητα στο πεδίο των τεχνών και τεχνολογιών του ήχου".
liveAudition: NO live audition. There IS an interview: "Υποψήφιοι … θα κληθούν για συνέντευξη από τις Επιτροπές Αξιολόγησης" — shortlisted candidates are called for interview by the evaluation committees. Portfolio is a supporting document reviewed on paper, not performed.
portfolioSpec: Portfolio required as supporting documentation, but the 2022-23 call does NOT publish a number-of-works, duration or file-format specification. UNVERIFIED as a precise build brief — the only hard spec published is the English certificate and the interview.
costForTunisian: Tuition (δίδακτρα) €2,700 for the whole programme, payable in instalments, per the 2022-23 call. No separate non-EU rate is published — Greek ΔΠΜΣ fees are the same for all nationalities. No registration or student-union fee published. PRIOR CYCLE figure; a new call could change it.
funding: The 2022-23 call publishes no scholarship. Greek ΔΠΜΣ law allows partial fee waivers for low-income students but nothing is published for this programme. Input's 'Partial' is UNVERIFIED — I found no funding instrument he could win here.
applicationDeadline: PRIOR CYCLE: "από την 1η Ιουλίου 2022 μέχρι και την 18η Σεπτεμβρίου 2022" — a July–September window with an 18 September 2022 close. No newer call exists. If revived, expect a summer window closing in September, which is far too late to start a September intake with a Tunisian student-visa process.
languageOfInstruction: Greek, with some English components; the thesis may be written in English. An English certificate is required: "Τίτλο πιστοποίησης τουλάχιστον καλής γνώσης της αγγλικής γλώσσας" (at least 'good knowledge', i.e. B2). He has no Greek.
verdictWhy: No call for applications has been published since 2022 — the programme looks dormant, and he cannot plan a 2027 intake around a call that has not appeared in four years. Even if revived, teaching is in Greek, which he does not speak, and the September deadline collides with the Greek student-visa timeline.
correction: STATUS: the input presents this as a live option.
